title: The Shape of an Old Grief

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older)

collection.description: A villager hears a laugh like that of someone they lost and finds themselves smiling: talk about them, or keep the smile.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Long ago, someone (subject) loved very much died. For years afterward, any reminder of them hurt so badly (subject.he/she) had to leave the room. Today (subject) hears someone laughing on the path, and the laugh sounds just like theirs, and (subject.he/she) notices that, for the first time, (subject.he/she) is smiling. It still hurts. It's just a different shape now.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells (friend) about the person: how they laughed, the terrible jokes they told, the way they always burned the fish. (friend) listens and asks questions. (subject) finds (subject.he/she) can talk about them for a long time without stopping. It's good to say their name out loud. Afterward (subject.he/she) is tired, and a little sad, and glad (subject.he/she) did it.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) doesn't tell anyone. (subject.He/she) just keeps walking, smiling a little, with the sound of that laugh in (subject.his/her) ears. It's still sore underneath. Maybe it always will be. But somewhere along the way, without (subject.him/her) noticing, missing them has turned into something (subject.he/she) can carry around without dropping everything else. (subject.He/she) doesn't know when that happened.
